docs.title: unrooted
docs.text:
Physics histogram analysis — without ROOT.

unrooted is a Python library for reading, manipulating, and visualising histograms from physics experiment data formats. It works entirely within the Python ecosystem using uproot and numpy — no ROOT installation required.

docs.title: Quick example
docs.text:
From a ROOT fileFrom boost-histogram 
from unrooted.io.root import load
from unrooted.plot.mpl import plot
from unrooted.plot import StyleSet

h = load("analysis.root", "hx")

ss = StyleSet.load("odd")
ax = plot(h, style=ss[0])
ax.figure.savefig("plot.png")

import pickle
from unrooted.io.boost import load
from unrooted.plot.mpl import plot
from unrooted.plot import StyleSet

with open("histograms.pkl", "rb") as f:
    data = pickle.load(f)

h = load(data["my_histogram"], name="my_histogram")

ss = StyleSet.load("odd")
ax = plot(h, style=ss[0])
ax.figure.savefig("plot.png")

docs.text: Module Purpose unrooted.io.root Read ROOT histograms (TH1, TH2, TProfile) and TTree branches unrooted.io.boost Convert boost_histogram objects (Mean, Double, Weight, …) unrooted.core Histogram and Axis — the common representation used by all backends unrooted.plot HistogramStyle, StyleSet — per-histogram and per-target theming unrooted.plot.mpl Matplotlib backend: plot, overlay, generate_stylesheet unrooted.plot.plotly Plotly backend: interactive plot and overlay returning go.Figure unrooted.plot.terminal Terminal backend: unicode plot and overlay returning str

docs.title: Logo concepts
docs.text:
Two SVG logo variants are provided for the library.

A — Histogram-Tree

B — u-monogram

Logo A — five histogram bars in a Gaussian bell-curve arrangement; three thin lines below the baseline represent roots being lifted. Colors follow the ODD palette.

Logo B — the letter u formed by two bars of different heights (navy + amber) connected at the bottom by a smooth arc. Each bar reads as a histogram bin; the whole shape reads as the initial of unrooted. Scales well to favicon size.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
unrooted converts ROOT files and boost-histogram objects into NumPy-backed data, then renders that data with independent plotting backends. ROOT I/O uses Uproot; no C++ ROOT installation is required.

ROOT histograms / branches         boost-histogram objects
             │                              │
     unrooted.io.root                unrooted.io.boost
             └──────────────┬───────────────┘
                            ▼
       unrooted.core: Axis / Histogram / ScatterData
                            │
             ┌──────────────┼───────────────┐
             ▼              ▼               ▼
         plot.mpl       plot.plotly     plot.terminal
       Matplotlib Axes  Plotly Figure       str
       hist + scatter   hist + scatter  histograms only

docs.title: Data contracts
docs.text:
Histogram contains axes, values, variances, optional flow values, and optional lower/upper spread bounds. Readers return independent snapshots; directly constructed objects may share the supplied arrays. Arrays are mutable, and public consumers validate them again. See the data contracts for shapes, NaNs, and ownership.

The interpretation of uncertainty depends on the reader:

Input Values Variances Spread bounds Count histogram Counts or weighted sums Count/weight variance None ROOT TProfile Mean Squared standard error from Uproot Mean ± reconstructed standard deviation Branch profile Mean Population variance / count Observed minimum and maximum Boost Mean Mean Sample variance / count Mean ± sample standard deviation Efficiency Passed / total Binomial variance Wilson confidence interval

ScatterData holds equally sized, flat real x/y arrays and labels. source_points, sample_seed, and sampled record optional sampling. Selection happens on tree entries before broadcasting and flattening paired branches. Without max_points, all selected pairs are retained. With sampling="random", a seeded uniform sample without replacement preserves pairing and input order. The ROOT guide explains chunking, multi-pass profiles, and memory limits.

docs.title: Supported input paths
docs.text:
Public reader Input Output unrooted.io.root.load TH1, TH2, TProfile Histogram unrooted.io.root.load_efficiency Separate unweighted passed/total TH1 objects Histogram unrooted.io.root.load_branch Numeric scalar, vector, or nested jagged branches Count/profile Histogram unrooted.io.root.load_scatter Two broadcast-compatible numeric branches ScatterData unrooted.io.boost.load Numeric Regular/Variable/Integer axes; Double/Int64/Unlimited/AtomicInt64/Weight/Mean storage Histogram unrooted.io.boost.load_efficiency Compatible 1D unweighted count histograms Histogram

TH3, TProfile2D, direct TEfficiency objects, categorical/Boolean boost axes, WeightedMean, and weighted efficiencies are unsupported. Histogram storage can represent more dimensions than the plotting backends render. See the I/O API and boost guide.

docs.title: Public plotting and composition
docs.text:
Import plot and overlay from unrooted.plot.mpl, unrooted.plot.plotly, or unrooted.plot.terminal. Graphical backends also export stack, plot_scatter, and overlay_scatter.

Matplotlib functions accept existing axes where documented. Its histogram overlay returns (main_axes, ratio_axes); the second value is None when no ratio is requested. Plotly functions return figures; plot_scatter accepts an existing figure and optional subplot row/column. Terminal functions return text. Ratio panels are histogram-only, require identical bin edges, and propagate uncertainties assuming independent inputs.

stack adds nonnegative 1D count/yield histograms with identical edges, in input order. Both graphical backends share validation and accumulation in plot/_stack.py. Layer thicknesses are the original values; the optional total uncertainty is sqrt(sum(variances)) for independent components. Profiles/efficiencies with spread bounds are rejected. Missing values leave gaps in the entire stack bin, and missing variances leave gaps in its total band.

HistogramStyle controls one dataset. StyleSet combines a packaged palette with style templates. The plotting guide and API reference describe arguments and backend capabilities.

docs.title: Module map
docs.text:
unrooted/
├── _version.py          sole release version, read by Hatchling
├── core/                axis, histogram, scatter, shared validation/statistics
├── io/
│   ├── root/            object readers, chunked branch loading, sampling
│   └── boost/           in-memory histogram conversion
├── plot/
│   ├── style.py         per-dataset appearance and named presets
│   ├── style_set.py     packaged palettes and coordinated styles
│   ├── mpl/             histogram/scatter rendering and stylesheet generation
│   ├── plotly/          optional interactive histogram/scatter rendering

Runtime resources are read with importlib.resources. Stylesheet generation writes to a caller-selected path or the current working directory. Adding a resource target requires a packaged colors.json containing four colors; logos are optional. See the resource guide.

docs.title: Supported configurations
docs.text:
The package requires Python 3.11 or newer. CI tests CPython 3.11–3.15 on Linux, plus 3.11 and 3.15 on macOS. Both ends of that range exercise the base installation without Plotly and a configuration with Plotly. Other Python versions and platforms are not currently covered by CI.

Dependency Minimum supported version NumPy 2.0 Uproot 5.6.0 Awkward Array 2.8.0 Matplotlib 3.8.4 boost-histogram 1.7.2 Plotly (optional) 5.24.1

These floors are tested together on Python 3.11. Newer Python versions use compatible versions from the lockfile; some minimum releases predate their interpreter and have no matching wheels. No speculative upper bounds are placed on runtime dependencies. Compatibility changes belong in release notes and require the same numerical and plotting regression checks. The NumPy floor also matches the NumPy 2 pickle format used by the checked-in boost-histogram fixture. Minimum-stack tests may report upstream Matplotlib deprecations; the open-figure resource warning is treated as an error.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
CI uses uv 0.13.5. Use that version to reproduce its environment and Python downloads. Development tools are defined once in the dev dependency group; the docs group includes it. Plotly remains a separate package extra.

git clone https://github.com/asalzburger/unrooted
cd unrooted
git lfs install
git lfs pull
uv sync --locked --python 3.11 --group docs --extra plotly

uv.lock is committed. --locked rejects dependency definitions that have not been resolved into it. Package consumers can still use pip and the declared dependency ranges; the lockfile is for contributors and CI.

docs.title: Required checks
docs.text:
Run from the checkout after the setup above. --no-sync keeps each command in the environment that was just selected. Isolated Python execution avoids imports from unrelated PYTHONPATH settings.

uv run --no-sync ruff check .
uv run --no-sync python -I -m pyright
uv run --no-sync python -I -m pytest -q
uv run --no-sync python -I tests/documentation/smoke.py
uv run --no-sync python -I -m mkdocs build --strict --site-dir /tmp/unrooted-docs-site
git diff --check
git status --short

Lint includes the package, tests, examples, benchmark harness, and docs hook. Pyright checks the package. The documentation smoke check executes the actual Python blocks in README and Getting Started, plus the README CLI examples, against synthetic ROOT and boost-histogram inputs. Browser display is intercepted; figures and HTML are exported. A strict documentation build also runs the gallery examples and checks API references.

Unit tests close Matplotlib figures and restore plotting settings after each test. Generated fixture/output files use temporary directories. Documentation gallery assets are generated in temporary storage and copied directly into the built site, leaving the source directory unchanged. CI requires an empty git status --porcelain after its checks.

docs.title: Dependency and environment checks
docs.text:
For ordinary code changes, keep uv.lock unchanged. To update dependencies:

uv lock --upgrade-package numpy
# Or deliberately refresh the complete dependency set:
uv lock --upgrade
uv sync --locked --group docs --extra plotly

Review the lockfile diff and run the required checks. Test supported interpreter boundaries and declared dependency floors before changing them. CI resolves the lowest allowed direct runtime dependencies in a separate environment while retaining its locked test tools. Transitive dependencies remain resolver-selected, so that job is intentionally separate from the reproducible locked matrix.

To reproduce that minimum-version job without altering your contributor environment:

UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/tmp/unrooted-minimum uv sync --locked --python 3.11
uv pip install --python /tmp/unrooted-minimum/bin/python \
  --resolution lowest-direct --upgrade -e '.[plotly]'
/tmp/unrooted-minimum/bin/python -I -m pytest -q

For a base environment, use a fresh UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT and run uv sync --locked --python 3.11 without --extra plotly. Plotly tests skip when the optional dependency is absent. The installed-wheel smoke check also verifies the missing-Plotly CLI diagnostic.

docs.title: Distribution checks
docs.text:
The build backend is included in the locked development tools. Build an sdist, then build the wheel from that sdist using those tools:

uv build --no-build-isolation --sdist --out-dir dist
uv build --no-build-isolation --wheel dist/*.tar.gz --out-dir dist
uv venv /tmp/unrooted-wheel
uv pip install --python /tmp/unrooted-wheel/bin/python dist/*.whl
/tmp/unrooted-wheel/bin/python -I tests/packaging/smoke.py
uv pip install --python /tmp/unrooted-wheel/bin/python 'unrooted[plotly]'
/tmp/unrooted-wheel/bin/python -I tests/packaging/smoke.py

The smoke script creates its own temporary working directory and data, checks that imports come from the installed wheel, and covers assets, statistical contracts, loading, Matplotlib export, and CLI behavior. With Plotly installed it also checks API and CLI HTML export. Static-image export requires the additional setup described in the CLI guide.

docs.title: Changes and pull requests
docs.text:
The release guide defines versioning, compatibility promises, candidate validation, and the separate publication procedure. The candidate workflow also runs the suite against the installed wheel across the support matrix, checks distribution metadata/assets, and validates generated links.

Use feat-<topic>, fix-<topic>, or chore-<topic> branches. Keep numerical references and user-facing documentation with behavior changes. Preserve the I/O → core → plotting separation, and use public APIs in examples. Run lint and type checking before committing. Describe the resulting behavior, validation, and any remaining limitations in the pull request.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
unrooted requires Python ≥ 3.11. The built-in palettes and logos are included in the installation. uv is optional for end users.

pipuv 
git clone https://github.com/asalzburger/unrooted
cd unrooted
python -m pip install .

git clone https://github.com/asalzburger/unrooted
cd unrooted
uv sync --no-dev

For interactive Plotly figures, use python -m pip install ".[plotly]" or uv sync --no-dev --extra plotly from the checkout. A built wheel can also be installed directly with python -m pip install /path/to/unrooted-<version>-py3-none-any.whl.

Contributors should use uv sync --locked --group docs --extra plotly and fetch the Git LFS test fixtures with git lfs install followed by git lfs pull. See the contributor workflow for the complete checks and support matrix.

docs.title: The common representation layer
docs.text:
Regardless of how a histogram enters unrooted, it becomes the same Histogram object:

from unrooted.core.histogram import Histogram
from unrooted.core.axis import Axis
import numpy as np

h = Histogram(
    axes=[Axis(edges=np.linspace(0, 10, 11), label="x [cm]")],
    values=np.array([1, 3, 5, 8, 10, 9, 7, 4, 2, 1], dtype=float),
    variances=np.array([1, 3, 5, 8, 10, 9, 7, 4, 2, 1], dtype=float),
    name="my_hist",
)

Histogram readers produce a Histogram; histogram plotting functions consume one. Point-cloud readers and scatter plotting functions use ScatterData. Switching between I/O backends or plot backends requires no changes to the code between them.

Attribute Meaning h.axes One Axis per dimension — edges, label, centers, widths h.values Bin counts or profile means h.variances Per-bin variance (Poisson counts or SE²) h.errors sqrt(variances) — ready for error bars h.overflow Values including under/overflow bins (when loaded) h.spread_min/max Per-bin spread band (profile and efficiency histograms)

docs.title: 1 — Load from a ROOT file
docs.text:
from unrooted.io.root import load

h = load("data.root", "hx")

print(h.name)               # "hx"
print(h.ndim)               # 1
print(h.values.shape)       # (n_bins,)
print(h.axes[0].centers)    # bin centres as numpy array

See Loading ROOT Data for TProfile, efficiency histograms, and TTree branches.

docs.title: 2 — Load from boost-histogram
docs.text:
unrooted.io.boost converts in-memory boost_histogram.Histogram objects produced by coffea, hand-filled analysis code, or any other framework that uses the boost-histogram API.

import pickle
from unrooted.io.boost import load, load_efficiency

with open("histograms.pkl", "rb") as f:
    data = pickle.load(f)

# Regular or weighted histogram
h = load(data["counts"], name="counts")

# Profile histogram (Mean storage)
prof = load(data["profile"], name="profile")

# Efficiency from accepted / total pair
eff = load_efficiency(data["accepted"], data["total"], name="trackeff")

See Loading boost-histogram Data for storage type details and multi-dimensional histograms.

docs.title: 3 — Plot it
docs.text:
from unrooted.plot.mpl import plot

ax = plot(h)
ax.figure.savefig("hx.png")

Pass a label to have it appear in the legend:

ax = plot(h, label="x distribution")
ax.legend()

docs.title: 4 — Apply a detector style
docs.text:
from unrooted.plot.mpl import plot
from unrooted.plot import StyleSet

ss = StyleSet.load("odd")   # or "sd"
ax = plot(h, style=ss[0])
ax.figure.savefig("hx_styled.png")

docs.title: 5 — Overlay multiple histograms
docs.text:
Histograms from different I/O backends can be overlaid directly — they share the same Histogram type:

from unrooted.io.root import load as load_root
from unrooted.io.boost import load as load_boost
from unrooted.plot.mpl import overlay
from unrooted.plot import StyleSet
import pickle

ss = StyleSet.load("odd")

h_root = load_root("data.root", "hx")
with open("histograms.pkl", "rb") as f:
    h_boost = load_boost(pickle.load(f)["hx"], name="hx_boost")

(ax, _) = overlay(
    [h_root, h_boost],
    labels=["ROOT", "boost"],
    styles=[ss[0], ss[1]],
)
ax.figure.savefig("overlay.png")

Add ratio=True to draw a ratio panel:

(ax_main, ax_ratio) = overlay([h_root, h_boost], labels=["ROOT", "boost"],
                               styles=[ss[0], ss[1]], ratio=True)

docs.title: 6 — Load a TTree branch
docs.text:
from unrooted.io.root import load_branch

# Count histogram
h = load_branch("data.root", "tree", "x", n_bins=50, range=(-5, 5))

# Profile histogram: mean(y) vs x
hp = load_branch("data.root", "tree", "x", "y")

See Loading ROOT Data for all supported branch types.

docs.title: 7 — Interactive Plotly figure
docs.text:
from unrooted.plot.plotly import plot, overlay

fig = plot(h)
fig.show()                         # opens in browser

fig2 = overlay([h_root, h_boost], labels=["ROOT", "boost"], ratio=True)
fig2.show()

Plotly is an optional dependency:

uv sync --extra plotly

docs.title: 8 — Quick terminal preview
docs.text:
No display needed — unrooted.plot.terminal renders directly to a unicode string:

from unrooted.plot.terminal import plot, overlay

print(plot(h))
print(overlay([h_root, h_boost], labels=["ROOT", "boost"]))

Useful for sanity-checking histograms in scripts, notebooks, SSH sessions, or CI logs.

docs.title: Release policy
docs.text:
The first candidate is 0.1.0rc1, licensed under MIT and maintained by Andreas Salzburger. GitHub Releases is the initial distribution destination; PyPI publication is deferred. Preparing a candidate or merging its pull request does not authorize publication.

The support promise covers the CPython 3.11–3.15 Linux/macOS configurations listed in the contributor guide, including base and Plotly installations and the declared minimum dependencies. It does not extend to Windows, untested platform/interpreter combinations, future dependency releases, long-term maintenance, or a response-time guarantee.

During 0.x, minor releases may introduce breaking changes when documented in the changelog. Patch releases preserve documented public APIs and CLI syntax, except that correctness fixes may reject invalid inputs or correct numerical results; such changes must be called out. Release candidates may change before the final release. Names beginning with _ and implementation helpers are private. The API reference and user guides define the public surface, including statistical semantics and CLI exit codes.

docs.title: Version and release notes
docs.text:
unrooted/_version.py is the only editable version source. Hatchling reads it without importing runtime dependencies; unrooted.__version__ imports the same value. Distribution metadata is checked against it. Use a v prefix for Git tags (for example v0.1.0rc1). Update CHANGELOG.md for every candidate, including compatibility changes, validation, and known limits. The lockfile records the project as dynamically versioned.

The sdist contains the package, license, README, changelog, and build configuration. It intentionally excludes test fixtures and the documentation build tree. Release tests and rendered documentation come from the same Git revision as the candidate.

docs.title: Candidate rehearsal
docs.text:
Start from a clean checkout with LFS fixtures and the locked contributor setup. Use a fresh output directory for each candidate; validation rejects multiple wheels or sdists. These commands do not publish anything:

uv sync --locked --group docs --extra plotly
uv run --no-sync ruff check .
uv run --no-sync python -I -m pyright
uv run --no-sync python -I -m pytest -q
uv build --no-build-isolation --sdist --out-dir /tmp/unrooted-candidate
uv build --no-build-isolation --wheel /tmp/unrooted-candidate/*.tar.gz --out-dir /tmp/unrooted-candidate
uv run --no-sync python -I tools/release/validate.py /tmp/unrooted-candidate --checksums --notes /tmp/unrooted-candidate/RELEASE_NOTES.md
uv venv --python 3.11 /tmp/unrooted-candidate-env
uv pip install --python /tmp/unrooted-candidate-env/bin/python /tmp/unrooted-candidate/*.whl
/tmp/unrooted-candidate-env/bin/python -I tests/packaging/smoke.py
uv pip install --python /tmp/unrooted-candidate-env/bin/python 'unrooted[plotly]'
/tmp/unrooted-candidate-env/bin/python -I tests/packaging/smoke.py
/tmp/unrooted-candidate-env/bin/python -I tests/documentation/smoke.py --installed
uv run --no-sync python -I -m mkdocs build --strict --site-dir /tmp/unrooted-candidate-site
uv run --no-sync python -I tests/documentation/links.py /tmp/unrooted-candidate-site

Repeat the installed-wheel rehearsal at the newest supported Python boundary. The Release candidate Actions workflow runs on pull requests and manual dispatches. It builds a wheel from the sdist once, validates version, license, README, dependencies, and every package file, then tests those same artifacts on the supported matrix and minimum stack. Tests use isolated Python and pytest's importlib mode to avoid importing the checkout. Plotly configurations also execute the actual introductory examples against the installed wheel. Checksums, release notes, distributions, and the built site are retained as Actions artifacts. Ordinary CI separately checks runtime-only wheel installs.

Inspect the generated site on desktop and narrow screens, including API signatures, tables, navigation, and example embeds. Inspect representative 1D/2D histograms, ratios, profiles, efficiencies, and scatter plots for labels, clipping, and uncertainty rendering. The link checker checks local pages, assets, and fragments; external links require a separate reachability check. Plotly static export is outside this matrix and remains a documented limitation.

docs.title: Preparing a draft and publishing
docs.text:
Only after an explicit release request:

  1. Review the candidate evidence and changelog, set the release date, and merge the reviewed changes. All required checks must pass for that revision.
  2. Create and push an annotated v<version> tag at that exact commit. Never move an already published tag or replace published artifacts.
  3. Run Release candidate manually on that tag with prepare_draft=true. It repeats validation and the installation matrix before creating a GitHub draft with the exact tested wheel, sdist, and SHA-256 manifest. A tag mismatch fails; an existing release is not overwritten. Pushing a tag alone does not publish or prepare a release.
  4. Inspect the draft notes/assets and candidate documentation artifact. Check the prerelease flag for rc versions, then publish the draft through GitHub only when the release request authorizes publication.
  5. Download the published artifacts into a fresh environment, verify their SHA-256 hashes, and repeat the installed-wheel smoke check. Record the release URL and validation outcome in the roadmap.

No package-index credentials or PyPI upload job are configured. Adding PyPI is a separate release-policy change. Failed rehearsal runs never reach the write-enabled draft job; normal PR/manual validation needs only read access.

docs.text: Import Axis from unrooted.core, and Histogram / ScatterData from unrooted or unrooted.core. Constructors validate inputs; arrays remain mutable. See data contracts for NaNs, flow bins, and ownership, and architecture for uncertainty semantics.

docs.title: Histogram dataclass
docs.text:
N-dimensional histogram with values, variances, and optional spread.

The central data structure of unrooted. Every I/O function returns a Histogram and every plot function accepts one. All numerical data is stored as numpy arrays so the object interops directly with the scientific Python ecosystem.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default axes list[Axis]

One :class:Axis per dimension, carrying bin edges and an optional axis label.

required values ndarray

Array of bin contents (counts or means for profile histograms). Shape: (n_bins,) for 1D, (nx, ny) for 2D.

required variances ndarray

Per-bin variance. For count histograms this equals values (Poisson); for profile histograms this is the squared standard error of the mean.

required name str

Optional histogram name (used as plot label fallback).

'' title str

Optional longer title.

'' overflow ndarray | None

Full values array with both flow slots per axis, shape (n_0 + 2, n_1 + 2, ...). Disabled flows are NaN. None if not loaded; edits to values do not synchronize it.

None spread_min ndarray | None

Optional lower spread bound. Branch profiles use the observed minimum; loaded profiles use mean minus standard deviation; efficiency readers use an interval bound.

None spread_max ndarray | None

Optional upper spread bound, paired with spread_min.

None Source code in unrooted/core/histogram.py 
@dataclass
class Histogram:
    """N-dimensional histogram with values, variances, and optional spread.

    The central data structure of *unrooted*.  Every I/O function returns a
    ``Histogram`` and every plot function accepts one.  All numerical data is
    stored as ``numpy`` arrays so the object interops directly with the
    scientific Python ecosystem.

    Args:
        axes:       One :class:`Axis` per dimension, carrying bin edges and
                    an optional axis label.
        values:     Array of bin contents (counts or means for profile
                    histograms).  Shape: ``(n_bins,)`` for 1D,
                    ``(nx, ny)`` for 2D.
        variances:  Per-bin variance.  For count histograms this equals
                    *values* (Poisson); for profile histograms this is the
                    squared standard error of the mean.
        name:       Optional histogram name (used as plot label fallback).
        title:      Optional longer title.
        overflow:   Full values array with both flow slots per axis, shape
                    ``(n_0 + 2, n_1 + 2, ...)``. Disabled flows are NaN.
                    ``None`` if not loaded; edits to values do not synchronize it.
        spread_min: Optional lower spread bound. Branch profiles use the
                    observed minimum; loaded profiles use mean minus standard
                    deviation; efficiency readers use an interval bound.
        spread_max: Optional upper spread bound, paired with ``spread_min``.
    """

    axes: list[Axis]
    values: np.ndarray
    variances: np.ndarray
    name: str = ""
    title: str = ""
    overflow: np.ndarray | None = field(default=None)
    spread_min: np.ndarray | None = field(default=None)
    spread_max: np.ndarray | None = field(default=None)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        self.validate()

    def validate(self) -> None:
        """Check dimensions, numeric domains, spread bounds, and full flow shape.

        Arrays are borrowed when no conversion is needed. Call after editing
        arrays; public plotting functions also validate before drawing.
        """
        if not isinstance(self.axes, (list, tuple)) or not self.axes:
            raise ValueError(
                "Histogram.axes must be a nonempty sequence of Axis objects"
            )
        if any(not isinstance(axis, Axis) for axis in self.axes):
            raise ValueError("Histogram.axes must contain only Axis objects")
        self.axes = list(self.axes)
        for axis in self.axes:
            axis.validate()
        expected = tuple(axis.n_bins for axis in self.axes)
        self.values = real_array(self.values, "Histogram.values")
        self.variances = real_array(self.variances, "Histogram.variances")
        if self.values.shape != expected:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Histogram.values shape {self.values.shape} must match axes {expected}"
            )
        if self.variances.shape != expected:
            raise ValueError("Histogram.variances must have the same shape as values")
        if np.any(self.variances < 0):
            raise ValueError("Histogram.variances must be nonnegative or NaN")
        if (self.spread_min is None) != (self.spread_max is None):
            raise ValueError(
                "Histogram spread_min and spread_max must be supplied together"
            )
        if self.spread_min is not None and self.spread_max is not None:
            self.spread_min = real_array(self.spread_min, "Histogram.spread_min")
            self.spread_max = real_array(self.spread_max, "Histogram.spread_max")
            if self.spread_min.shape != expected or self.spread_max.shape != expected:
                raise ValueError(
                    "Histogram spread bounds must have the same shape as values"
                )
            if not np.array_equal(np.isnan(self.spread_min), np.isnan(self.spread_max)):
                raise ValueError(
                    "Histogram spread bounds must have matching NaN positions"
                )
            if np.any(self.spread_min > self.spread_max):
                raise ValueError("Histogram spread_min must not exceed spread_max")
            if np.any(self.spread_min > self.values) or np.any(
                self.spread_max < self.values
            ):
                raise ValueError("Histogram spread bounds must enclose finite values")
        if self.overflow is not None:
            self.overflow = real_array(self.overflow, "Histogram.overflow")
            flow_shape = tuple(n + 2 for n in expected)
            if self.overflow.shape != flow_shape:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Histogram.overflow shape must be {flow_shape}, "
                    "including both flow bins"
                )

    def require_compatible_binning(self, other: Histogram) -> None:

def validate(self) -> None:
    """Check dimensions, numeric domains, spread bounds, and full flow shape.

    Arrays are borrowed when no conversion is needed. Call after editing
    arrays; public plotting functions also validate before drawing.
    """
    if not isinstance(self.axes, (list, tuple)) or not self.axes:
        raise ValueError(
            "Histogram.axes must be a nonempty sequence of Axis objects"
        )
    if any(not isinstance(axis, Axis) for axis in self.axes):
        raise ValueError("Histogram.axes must contain only Axis objects")
    self.axes = list(self.axes)
    for axis in self.axes:
        axis.validate()
    expected = tuple(axis.n_bins for axis in self.axes)
    self.values = real_array(self.values, "Histogram.values")
    self.variances = real_array(self.variances, "Histogram.variances")
    if self.values.shape != expected:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Histogram.values shape {self.values.shape} must match axes {expected}"
        )
    if self.variances.shape != expected:
        raise ValueError("Histogram.variances must have the same shape as values")
    if np.any(self.variances < 0):
        raise ValueError("Histogram.variances must be nonnegative or NaN")
    if (self.spread_min is None) != (self.spread_max is None):
        raise ValueError(
            "Histogram spread_min and spread_max must be supplied together"
        )
    if self.spread_min is not None and self.spread_max is not None:
        self.spread_min = real_array(self.spread_min, "Histogram.spread_min")
        self.spread_max = real_array(self.spread_max, "Histogram.spread_max")
        if self.spread_min.shape != expected or self.spread_max.shape != expected:
            raise ValueError(
                "Histogram spread bounds must have the same shape as values"
            )
        if not np.array_equal(np.isnan(self.spread_min), np.isnan(self.spread_max)):
            raise ValueError(
                "Histogram spread bounds must have matching NaN positions"
            )
        if np.any(self.spread_min > self.spread_max):
            raise ValueError("Histogram spread_min must not exceed spread_max")
        if np.any(self.spread_min > self.values) or np.any(
            self.spread_max < self.values
        ):
            raise ValueError("Histogram spread bounds must enclose finite values")
    if self.overflow is not None:
        self.overflow = real_array(self.overflow, "Histogram.overflow")
        flow_shape = tuple(n + 2 for n in expected)
        if self.overflow.shape != flow_shape:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Histogram.overflow shape must be {flow_shape}, "
                "including both flow bins"
            )

class Axis:
    """One axis of a histogram, described by its bin edges.

    Args:
        edges: Array of ``n_bins + 1`` monotonically increasing bin-edge
               values.  The first and last entries are the left edge of the
               first bin and the right edge of the last bin respectively.
        label: Human-readable axis label used as a plot axis title.
    """

    edges: np.ndarray
    label: str = ""

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        self.validate()

    def validate(self) -> None:
        """Require finite, strictly increasing, one-dimensional float64 edges."""
        self.edges = real_array(self.edges, "Axis.edges", allow_nan=False, dtype=float)
        if self.edges.ndim != 1 or self.edges.size < 2:
            raise ValueError("Axis.edges must be 1D with at least two edges")
        if np.any(self.edges[1:] <= self.edges[:-1]):
            raise ValueError("Axis.edges must be strictly increasing")

    @property
    def n_bins(self) -> int:
        """Number of bins (``len(edges) - 1``)."""
        return len(self.edges) - 1

    @property
    def centers(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """Array of bin-centre coordinates, shape ``(n_bins,)``."""
        return 0.5 * self.edges[:-1] + 0.5 * self.edges[1:]

    @property
    def widths(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """Array of bin widths, shape ``(n_bins,)``."""
        return self.edges[1:] - self.edges[:-1]

class ScatterData:
    """Raw (x, y) point cloud read from two TTree branches.

    Unlike :class:`~unrooted.core.histogram.Histogram`, this type carries
    un-binned data and is rendered as a scatter plot rather than a step
    function.

    Attributes:
        x:       Flat array of x-values (already broadcast and flattened).
        y:       Flat array of y-values, same length as *x*.
        name:    Logical name (typically the y-branch name).
        x_label: Axis label for x (defaults to the x-branch name).
        y_label: Axis label for y (defaults to the y-branch name).
        title:   Optional figure title.
        source_points: Number of flattened pairs before optional sampling.
        sample_seed: RNG seed when random sampling was requested.
    """

    x: np.ndarray
    y: np.ndarray
    name: str = ""
    x_label: str = ""
    y_label: str = ""
    title: str = ""
    source_points: int | None = None
    sample_seed: int | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        self.validate()

    def validate(self) -> None:
        """Require flat, equally sized real arrays; NaNs are retained as gaps."""
        self.x = real_array(self.x, "ScatterData.x")
        self.y = real_array(self.y, "ScatterData.y")
        if self.x.ndim != 1 or self.y.ndim != 1:
            raise ValueError("ScatterData x and y must be 1D arrays")
        if len(self.x) != len(self.y):
            raise ValueError(
                f"ScatterData x and y must have the same length, "
                f"got {len(self.x)} and {len(self.y)}"
            )
        for name, value in (
            ("source_points", self.source_points),
            ("sample_seed", self.sample_seed),
        ):
            if value is not None and (
                isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, Integral) or value < 0
            ):
                raise ValueError(f"ScatterData.{name} must be a nonnegative integer")
        if self.source_points is not None and self.source_points < len(self.x):
            raise ValueError(
                "ScatterData.source_points must be at least the retained size"
            )
        if self.sample_seed is not None and self.source_points is None:
            raise ValueError("ScatterData.sample_seed requires source_points")

    @property
    def sampled(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the reader retained fewer pairs than its selected source."""
        return self.source_points is not None and len(self.x) < self.source_points

def load_efficiency(
    path: str | Path,
    pass_key: str,
    total_key: str,
    *,
    confidence_level: float = DEFAULT_CONFIDENCE_LEVEL,
) -> Histogram:
    """Compute a binomial efficiency from separate passed and total TH1 objects.

    Requires 1D unweighted, finite, nonnegative integer counts with passed <=
    total, Poisson-compatible variances, and exactly identical edges. Profiles,
    TH2, and TEfficiency objects are unsupported.

    Values are passed/total, variances retain p*(1-p)/total, and spread bounds
    are Wilson intervals without continuity correction (68.268949% by default).
    All four arrays contain NaN for bins with zero total. Endpoint intervals
    have nonzero width, even though the variance field is zero there.

    Args:
        path: Path to the ROOT file.
        pass_key: Key counting passing events.
        total_key: Key counting total events.
        confidence_level: Nominal Wilson confidence level, strictly between 0 and 1.

    Raises:
        KeyError: If either key is absent.
        ValueError: If inputs, binning, or confidence level are unsupported.
    """
    with cast(Any, uproot.open(path)) as f:
        if any(
            not f.classname_of(key).startswith("TH1") for key in (pass_key, total_key)
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                "Efficiency inputs must be one-dimensional TH1 count histograms"
            )

            _from_root(f[pass_key], pass_key),
            _from_root(f[total_key], total_key),
            confidence_level=confidence_level,
        )

def load_branch(
    path: str | Path,
    key: str,
    x_branch: str,
    y_branch: str | None = None,
    *,
    n_bins: int = 100,
    range: tuple[float, float] | None = None,  # noqa: A002
    label: str = "",
    entry_start: int = 0,
    entry_stop: int | None = None,
    step_size: int = DEFAULT_STEP_SIZE,
) -> Histogram:
    """Load selected tree entries as a count or population-profile histogram.

    Scalars, vectors, and nested jagged branches are flattened. Profile pairs
    are aligned with awkward.broadcast_arrays within each chunk. Bins are
    [left, right), including the final right edge. Out-of-range x is omitted.

    Count histograms need one accumulation pass. Profiles use three passes:
    observed extrema/counts, sums shifted by the global per-bin minima, and
    centered squared deviations. This preserves numerical stability at large
    offsets without retaining all observations. Automatic ranges require an
    additional x-only pass before broadcasting.

    Profile variance is M2/N². Empty bins have value/variance zero and NaN
    extrema; single-entry bins have zero variance and equal extrema.

    Args:
        path: ROOT file path.
        key: Tree path inside the file.
        x_branch: Branch defining the bin axis.
        y_branch: Optional branch to profile against x.
        n_bins: Positive number of bins (default 100).
        range: Finite (lo, hi), lo < hi; None scans the selected x values.
        label: X-axis label; defaults to x_branch.
        entry_start: First entry included, nonnegative (default zero).
        entry_stop: First entry excluded; None reads to the end. Bounds beyond
                    the tree length are clipped. Selection precedes flattening.
        step_size: Maximum entries per chunk (default 100,000). This is not a
                   byte limit; jagged expansion and ROOT baskets affect memory.
    """
    _validate_entries(entry_start, entry_stop)
    _positive_integer(step_size, "step_size")
    _positive_integer(n_bins, "n_bins")
    with cast(Any, uproot.open)(path, array_cache=None) as root_file:
        tree = _get_tree(root_file, key, x_branch, y_branch)
        bounds = _range(tree, x_branch, range, entry_start, entry_stop, step_size)
        axis = Axis(np.linspace(*bounds, int(n_bins) + 1), label=label or x_branch)
        if y_branch is None:
            counts = np.zeros(axis.n_bins, dtype=np.int64)
            for x, _ in _chunks(
                tree, x_branch, None, entry_start, entry_stop, step_size
            ):
                counts += np.histogram(x, bins=axis.edges)[0]
            values = counts.astype(float)
            return Histogram([axis], values, values.copy(), name=x_branch)
        return _profile(
            tree, x_branch, y_branch, axis, entry_start, entry_stop, step_size
        )

def load_scatter(
    path: str | Path,
    key: str,
    x_branch: str,
    y_branch: str,
    *,
    label_x: str = "",
    label_y: str = "",
    entry_start: int = 0,
    entry_stop: int | None = None,
    step_size: int = DEFAULT_STEP_SIZE,
    max_points: int | None = None,
    sampling: str = "error",
    seed: int = 0,
) -> ScatterData:
    """Load point pairs in chunks, with an optional explicit limit or sample.

    Entry selection precedes awkward broadcasting and flattening. Without
    max_points all selected pairs are returned, so result memory grows with
    the selection. No sampling happens implicitly.

    Args:
        path: ROOT file path.
        key: Tree path inside the file.
        x_branch: Branch for x coordinates.
        y_branch: Branch for y coordinates.
        label_x: X-axis label; defaults to x_branch.
        label_y: Y-axis label; defaults to y_branch.
        entry_start: First entry included, nonnegative (default zero).
        entry_stop: First entry excluded; None reads to the end. Bounds beyond
                    the tree length are clipped.
        step_size: Maximum entries per chunk, not bytes (default 100,000).
        max_points: Positive maximum retained pairs, or None for all pairs.
        sampling: 'error' raises when max_points is exceeded. 'random' retains
                  a uniform sample without replacement over flattened pairs;
                  requires max_points. Returned points keep their input order.
        seed: Nonnegative RNG seed (default zero), used by random sampling.
              Results repeat for the same data/seed across chunk sizes.
    """
    _validate_entries(entry_start, entry_stop)
    _positive_integer(step_size, "step_size")
    if max_points is not None:
        _positive_integer(max_points, "max_points")
    if sampling not in ("error", "random"):
        raise ValueError("sampling must be 'error' or 'random'")
    if sampling == "random" and max_points is None:
        raise ValueError("sampling='random' requires max_points")
    if isinstance(seed, bool) or not isinstance(seed, Integral) or seed < 0:
        raise ValueError("seed must be a nonnegative integer")
    if sampling != "random" and seed != 0:
        raise ValueError("seed is only used with sampling='random'")
    accumulator = ScatterAccumulator(max_points, sampling, int(seed))
    with cast(Any, uproot.open)(path, array_cache=None) as root_file:
        tree = _get_tree(root_file, key, x_branch, y_branch)
        for x, y in _chunks(
            tree, x_branch, y_branch, entry_start, entry_stop, step_size
        ):
            assert y is not None
            accumulator.add(x, y)
    x, y = accumulator.finish()
    return ScatterData(
        x=x,
        y=y,
        name=y_branch,
        x_label=label_x or x_branch,
        y_label=label_y or y_branch,
        source_points=accumulator.total,
        sample_seed=int(seed) if sampling == "random" else None,
    )

def load(hist: bh.Histogram, name: str = "") -> Histogram:
    """Convert a boost-histogram :class:`~boost_histogram.Histogram` to an
    unrooted :class:`~unrooted.core.Histogram`.

    Supports numeric ``Regular``, ``Variable``, and ``Integer`` axes and the
    following storage types:

    * ``Mean`` — treated as a profile histogram; populates ``spread_min`` /
      ``spread_max`` as mean ± σ_y (standard deviation of individual
      measurements).  Empty bins (count = 0) get ``nan`` spread.
    * ``Weight`` — structured storage with ``value`` and ``variance`` fields.
    * ``Double``, ``Int64``, ``Unlimited``, ``AtomicInt64`` — Poisson assumption;
      ``variances`` equals ``values``.

    Categorical/Boolean axes and ``WeightedMean`` storage are unsupported.
    Arrays are independent snapshots of the source. Missing flow slots are
    padded with NaN. Axis metadata strings become axis labels.

    Args:
        hist: The boost-histogram histogram to convert.
        name: Name assigned to the returned histogram.

    Returns:
        A :class:`~unrooted.core.Histogram` populated from *hist*.
    """
    if hist.ndim == 0:
        raise ValueError("Boost histogram must have at least one numeric axis")
    for ax in hist.axes:
        if not isinstance(ax, (bh.axis.Regular, bh.axis.Variable, bh.axis.Integer)):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unsupported boost axis {type(ax).__name__}; "
                "use numeric Regular, Variable, or Integer axes"
            )
    if hist.storage_type not in (*_COUNT_STORAGES, bh.storage.Weight, bh.storage.Mean):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unsupported boost storage {hist.storage_type.__name__}; "
            "use count, Weight, or Mean storage; WeightedMean is unsupported"
        )
    axes = [
        Axis(edges=np.array(ax.edges, copy=True), label=_axis_label(ax))
        for ax in hist.axes
    ]

    if hist.storage_type == bh.storage.Mean:
        view: Any = hist.view(flow=False)
        count = np.asarray(view["count"])
        values = np.array(view["value"], copy=True)
        sod2 = np.asarray(view["_sum_of_deltas_squared"])

        has_data = count > 0
        safe_count = np.where(count >= 2, count, 1.0)
        safe_count_m1 = np.where(count >= 2, count - 1, 1.0)

        # SE² = sod2 / (count * (count-1)); 0 for bins with 0 or 1 entries
        variances = np.where(
            count >= 2,
            np.maximum(0.0, sod2) / (safe_count * safe_count_m1),
            0.0,
        )

        # σ_y = std-dev of individual measurements; NaN for empty bins
        sigma_y = np.where(
            has_data,
            np.where(count >= 2, np.sqrt(np.maximum(0.0, sod2 / safe_count_m1)), 0.0),
            np.nan,
        )

        spread_min: np.ndarray | None = np.where(has_data, values - sigma_y, np.nan)
        spread_max: np.ndarray | None = np.where(has_data, values + sigma_y, np.nan)
        overflow_view: Any = hist.view(flow=True)
        overflow = _flow_values(hist, overflow_view["value"])

        return Histogram(
            axes=axes,
            values=values,
            variances=variances,
            name=name,
            overflow=overflow,
            spread_min=spread_min,
            spread_max=spread_max,
        )

    raw: Any = hist.view(flow=False)
    raw_flow: Any = hist.view(flow=True)
    if hist.storage_type == bh.storage.Weight:
        # Weight storage
        values = np.array(raw["value"], dtype=float, copy=True)
        variances = np.array(raw["variance"], dtype=float, copy=True)
        overflow = _flow_values(hist, raw_flow["value"])
    else:
        values = np.array(raw, dtype=float, copy=True)
        variances = values.copy()
        overflow = _flow_values(hist, raw_flow)

    return Histogram(
        axes=axes,
        values=values,
        variances=variances,
        name=name,
        overflow=overflow,
    )

def load_efficiency(
    accepted: bh.Histogram,
    total: bh.Histogram,
    name: str = "",
    *,
    confidence_level: float = DEFAULT_CONFIDENCE_LEVEL,
) -> Histogram:
    """Compute per-bin efficiency from two boost-histogram histograms.

    The returned :class:`~unrooted.core.Histogram` contains:

    * ``values``    — efficiency = accepted / total per bin (``nan`` for empty)
    * ``variances`` — binomial variance = eff × (1 − eff) / total
    * ``spread_min/max`` — Wilson interval without continuity correction

    The default confidence level is 68.268949%. Bins where *total* = 0
    receive ``nan`` for values, variances, and interval bounds. Only 1D,
    unweighted, finite, nonnegative integer counts with accepted <= total
    and exactly identical edges are supported.

    Args:
        accepted: Histogram counting accepted (passing) events.
        total:    Histogram counting all (total) events.
        name:     Name assigned to the returned histogram.
        confidence_level: Nominal Wilson confidence level, strictly between 0 and 1.

    Returns:
        A :class:`~unrooted.core.Histogram` representing the efficiency.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If inputs, storage, binning, or confidence level are unsupported.
    """
    for hist in (accepted, total):
        if hist.storage_type not in _COUNT_STORAGES:
            raise ValueError(
                "Efficiency inputs require unweighted count storage "
                "(Double, Int64, Unlimited, or AtomicInt64); "
                "Weight, Mean, and WeightedMean are unsupported"
            )
        if hist.variances(flow=False) is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "Efficiency inputs require known unweighted count variances; "
                "weighted scalar fills are unsupported"
            )
    return binomial_efficiency(
        load(accepted),
        load(total),
        name=name,
        confidence_level=confidence_level,
    )

@dataclass
class HistogramStyle:
    """Visual style for a single 1D histogram.

    All ``*_color`` fields accept matplotlib-style color spec (named string,
    hex, or RGBA tuple).  ``None`` means "inherit the automatic cycle color".
    ``*_alpha`` fields are applied on top of whatever alpha is encoded in the
    color itself.

    Prefer the named constructors over building this manually:

    * :meth:`as_hist`        — step fill + error bars (count histogram default)
    * :meth:`as_stack`       — filled stack component + outline
    * :meth:`as_line`        — step line only, no fill, no errors
    * :meth:`as_markers`     — markers at bin centres + error bars
    * :meth:`as_efficiency`  — markers + error bars + spread band
    * :meth:`as_profile`     — line + spread band (TProfile)

    ``error_display`` and ``spread_display`` each accept ``"bar"`` (error bars
    at bin centres), ``"band"`` (step-shaped filled area following bin edges),
    or ``"continuous"`` (smooth filled envelope connecting bin centres).
    """

    # --- Line (step function) ---
    line_color: str | tuple[float, ...] | None = None  # None → auto cycle
    line_alpha: float = 1.0
    line_style: str | None = "-"    # None → no line; "-", "--", ":", "-."
    line_width: float = 1.5

    # --- Marker (at bin centres) ---
    marker: str | None = None                           # None → no marker
    marker_color: str | tuple[float, ...] | None = None # None → same as line
    marker_alpha: float = 1.0
    marker_size: float = 5.0

    # --- Fill (under the step function) ---
    fill_color: str | tuple[float, ...] | None = None   # None → same as line
    fill_alpha: float | None = None                     # None → no fill
    fill_hatch: str | None = None                       # e.g. "/", "x", "."

    # --- Error display (bin ± sqrt(variance)) ---
    error_display: Literal["bar", "band", "continuous"] | None = "bar"
    error_color: str | tuple[float, ...] | None = None  # None → same as line
    error_alpha: float = 0.4                      # opacity for "band" / "continuous"
    error_capsize: float = 2.0                          # cap size for "bar"

    # --- Spread display (Histogram.spread_min / spread_max) ---
    spread_display: Literal["bar", "band", "continuous"] | None = None
    spread_color: str | tuple[float, ...] | None = None # None → same as line
    spread_alpha: float = 0.15
    spread_capsize: float = 2.0

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Named constructors
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    @classmethod
    def as_stack(cls, **overrides) -> HistogramStyle:
        """Filled stack component with an outline; errors belong to the total."""
        return cls(**{
            "line_style": LineStyle.SOLID,
            "fill_alpha": 0.8,
            "marker": None,
            "error_display": None,
            "spread_display": None,
            **overrides,
        })

    @classmethod
    def as_hist(cls, **overrides) -> HistogramStyle:
        """Step-function histogram with fill and error bars.

        The typical appearance for a count histogram: filled step area at low
        opacity with error bars at each bin centre.
        """
        return cls(**{
            "line_style": LineStyle.SOLID,
            "fill_alpha": 0.15,
            "error_display": "bar",
            "spread_display": None,
            **overrides,
        })

    @classmethod
    def as_line(cls, **overrides) -> HistogramStyle:
        """Step line only — no fill, no markers, no error display."""
        return cls(**{
            "line_style": LineStyle.SOLID,
            "fill_alpha": None,
            "marker": None,
            "error_display": None,
            "spread_display": None,
            **overrides,
        })

    @classmethod
    def as_markers(cls, **overrides) -> HistogramStyle:
        """Markers at bin centres with error bars, no step line."""
        return cls(**{
            "line_style": None,
            "marker": "o",
            "fill_alpha": None,
            "error_display": "bar",
            "spread_display": None,
            **overrides,
        })

    @classmethod
    def as_efficiency(cls, **overrides) -> HistogramStyle:
        """Markers + error bars + spread band — suited for efficiency histograms."""
        return cls(**{
            "line_style": None,
            "marker": "o",
            "fill_alpha": None,
            "error_display": "bar",
            "spread_display": "band",
            "spread_alpha": 0.15,
            **overrides,
        })

    @classmethod
    def as_profile(cls, **overrides) -> HistogramStyle:
        """Step line + spread band — suited for TProfile histograms."""
        return cls(**{
            "line_style": LineStyle.SOLID,
            "fill_alpha": None,
            "marker": None,
            "error_display": "bar",
            "spread_display": "band",
            "spread_alpha": 0.15,
            **overrides,
        })

    @classmethod
    def as_scatter(cls, **overrides) -> HistogramStyle:
        """Tiny point markers — suited for 2D scatter plots from TTree branches."""
        return cls(**{
            "line_style": None,
            "marker": ".",
            "marker_size": 2.0,
            "fill_alpha": None,
            "error_display": None,
            "spread_display": None,
            **overrides,
        })

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Copy helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def with_color(
        self,
        color: str | tuple[float, ...],
        *,
        override_explicit: bool = False,
    ) -> HistogramStyle:
        """Return a copy with *color* applied to all colour fields that are ``None``.

        By default only fields that are currently ``None`` are set, so any
        explicitly chosen colours are preserved.  Pass
        ``override_explicit=True`` to replace *all* colour fields regardless.

        Args:
            color:            Matplotlib color spec (hex string, named color,
                              or RGBA tuple).
            override_explicit: When ``True``, overwrite every ``*_color``
                              field unconditionally.
        """
        color_fields = (
            "line_color",
            "marker_color",
            "fill_color",
            "error_color",
            "spread_color",
        )
        updates: dict[str, str | tuple[float, ...]] = {}
        for f in color_fields:
            if override_explicit or getattr(self, f) is None:
                updates[f] = color
        return dataclasses.replace(self, **updates)

@dataclass
class StyleSet:
    """A coordinated set of histogram styles tied to a resource target.

    Each style combines a color from the target's ``colors.json`` palette with
    shape properties from a :class:`StyleTemplate`.  Up to four styles are
    available by default; the index wraps cyclically so you never run out when
    overlaying more than four histograms.

    Use :meth:`load` to build a ``StyleSet`` from a resource target name.
    Index with ``style_set[i]``.
    """

    name: str
    description: str
    colors: list[str]             # 4 hex strings
    styles: list[HistogramStyle]  # assembled HistogramStyle objects

    @classmethod
    def load(
        cls,
        target: str,
        *,
        templates: list[StyleTemplate] | None = None,
        show_errors: bool = True,
        show_spread: bool = False,
    ) -> StyleSet:
        """Load a palette bundled in ``unrooted/resources/{target}/colors.json``.

        Args:
            target:      Resource target name, e.g. ``"odd"`` or ``"sd"``.
            templates:   Override the default four :data:`DEFAULT_STYLE_TEMPLATES`.
                         The list length determines how many styles are created;
                         it must match the number of colors in the palette or be
                         shorter.
            show_errors: When ``False``, sets ``error_display=None`` on every
                         style regardless of the template setting.
            show_spread: When ``True``,  sets ``spread_display="band"`` on every
                         style regardless of the template setting.

        Raises:
            FileNotFoundError: When no ``colors.json`` exists for *target*.
        """
        palette = files("unrooted").joinpath("resources", target, "colors.json")
        data: dict[str, Any] = json.loads(palette.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        colors: list[str] = data["colors"]

        tmpl_list = templates if templates is not None else DEFAULT_STYLE_TEMPLATES

        styles: list[HistogramStyle] = []
        for color, tmpl in zip(colors, tmpl_list):
            error_display = tmpl.error_display if show_errors else None
            spread_display = "band" if show_spread else tmpl.spread_display
            styles.append(
                HistogramStyle(
                    line_color=color,
                    line_style=tmpl.line_style,
                    line_width=tmpl.line_width,
                    marker=tmpl.marker,
                    marker_color=color,
                    marker_size=tmpl.marker_size,
                    fill_color=color,
                    fill_alpha=tmpl.fill_alpha,
                    error_color=color,
                    error_display=error_display,
                    spread_color=color,
                    spread_display=spread_display,
                )
            )

        return cls(
            name=data["name"],
            description=data["description"],
            colors=colors,
            styles=styles,
        )

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self.styles)

    def __getitem__(self, i: int) -> HistogramStyle:
        return self.styles[i % len(self.styles)]

def stack(
    hists: list[Histogram],
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    labels: list[str] | None = None,
    styles: list[HistogramStyle] | None = None,
    *,
    uncertainty: bool = True,
) -> Axes:
    """Stack additive 1D histograms in input order, first at the bottom.

    Requires exactly matching bin edges and nonnegative values. Profiles and
    efficiencies with spread bounds are rejected. A NaN value in any component
    leaves a gap in every layer of that bin; NaN variances leave gaps only in
    the total uncertainty band. Flow bins are not drawn. Inputs are not rebinned,
    normalized, or modified. Weighted yields are allowed when bins are nonnegative.

    Args:
        hists: Nonempty list of additive count/yield histograms.
        ax: Existing axes, or None to create a figure.
        labels: Optional legend labels in input order, one per component.
        styles: Per-component fill and line settings; defaults to as_stack().
            Marker, error, and spread settings do not apply to stack components.
            Supported hatches are /, backslash, x, -, |, +, and dot.
        uncertainty: Draw total ± sqrt(sum(variances)) as a gray band. This
            assumes independent components and includes no covariance. The band
            is not clipped at zero and is labeled when component labels are given.

    Returns:
        The Matplotlib axes, suitable for additional data overlays.

    Raises:
        ValueError: For incompatible bins, negative values, non-additive inputs,
            mismatched labels/styles, or nonrepresentable cumulative sums.
    """
    colors = plt.rcParams["axes.prop_cycle"].by_key()["color"]
    data = prepare_stack(hists, labels, styles, colors, uncertainty)
    if ax is None:
        _, ax = plt.subplots()
    for i, style in enumerate(data.styles):
        label = labels[i] if labels is not None else None
        if style.fill_alpha is not None:
            ax.stairs(
                data.upper[i],
                data.edges,
                baseline=data.lower[i],
                fill=True,
                facecolor=style.fill_color,
                edgecolor=style.line_color,
                linewidth=0,
                alpha=style.fill_alpha,
                hatch=style.fill_hatch,
                label=label,
            )
            label = None
        if style.line_style is not None:
            ax.stairs(
                data.upper[i],
                data.edges,
                baseline=None,
                color=style.line_color,
                alpha=style.line_alpha,
                linewidth=style.line_width,
                linestyle=style.line_style,
                label=label,
            )
    if uncertainty:
        x = np.repeat(data.edges, 2)[1:-1]
        total = data.upper[-1]
        ax.fill_between(
            x,
            np.repeat(total - data.errors, 2),
            np.repeat(total + data.errors, 2),
            color="#303030",
            alpha=0.25,
            linewidth=0,
            label="Total ±1σ" if labels is not None else None,
        )
    if hists[0].axes[0].label:
        ax.set_xlabel(hists[0].axes[0].label)
    if hists[0].title:
        ax.set_title(hists[0].title)
    if labels is not None:
        ax.legend()
    return ax

def generate_stylesheet(
    target: str,
    output: Path | str | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Render a style-palette preview PNG to a user-writable destination.

    Produces a single plot with four overlaid synthetic Gaussian histograms —
    one per style slot — so the color, line, marker, fill, and error-bar
    choices can be reviewed at a glance.

    Args:
        target: Resource target name, e.g. ``"odd"`` or ``"sd"``.
        output: Destination path. Defaults to ``{target}_stylesheet.png`` in
                the current working directory. The parent directory must exist.

    Returns:
        The output path, retaining a relative path when one was supplied.
    """
    import matplotlib

    matplotlib.use("Agg")
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

    from unrooted.plot.mpl.overlay import overlay

    style_set = StyleSet.load(target)

    hists = [_gaussian_histogram(i) for i in range(4)]
    labels = [
        f"Style {i + 1}  —  {style_set.colors[i]}" for i in range(4)
    ]
    styles = [style_set[i] for i in range(4)]

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5))
    overlay(hists, ax=ax, labels=labels, styles=styles)
    ax.set_title(f"{target.upper()} style palette", fontsize=13, fontweight="bold")

    out = Path(output) if output is not None else Path(f"{target}_stylesheet.png")
    try:
        fig.savefig(out, dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
    finally:
        plt.close(fig)
    return out

def stack(
    hists: list[Histogram],
    labels: list[str] | None = None,
    styles: list[HistogramStyle] | None = None,
    *,
    uncertainty: bool = True,
) -> go.Figure:
    """Stack additive 1D histograms in input order, first at the bottom.

    Requires identical edges, nonnegative values, and no profile/efficiency
    spread bounds. Missing values make the whole bin a gap; missing variances
    make only the total band a gap. Flow bins are omitted. Inputs are not
    modified, normalized, or rebinned. Nonnegative weighted yields are supported.

    Args:
        hists: Nonempty list of additive count/yield histograms.
        labels: Optional legend labels in input order, one per component.
        styles: Per-component fill and line settings; defaults to as_stack().
            Marker/error/spread settings do not apply to components. Supported
            hatches are /, backslash, x, -, |, +, and dot. Use hex/RGBA colors
            for consistent opacity across backends.
        uncertainty: Draw total ± sqrt(sum(variances)), assuming independent
            components with no covariance. The band is not clipped at zero.

    Returns:
        A Plotly figure. Legend toggles hide a component's drawing; they do not
        recompute other layers or the uncertainty of the original full sum.

    Raises:
        ValueError: For incompatible bins, negative values, spread bounds,
            mismatched labels/styles, or nonrepresentable cumulative sums.
    """
    data = prepare_stack(hists, labels, styles, DEFAULT_COLORS, uncertainty)
    fig = go.Figure()
    for i, style in enumerate(data.styles):
        x, upper = _staircase(data.edges, data.upper[i])
        _, lower = _staircase(data.edges, data.lower[i])
        label = labels[i] if labels is not None else None
        group = f"stack-{i}"
        if style.fill_alpha is not None:
            assert style.fill_color is not None
            _add_fill(
                fig,
                x,
                lower,
                upper,
                _to_rgba(style.fill_color, style.fill_alpha),
                label,
                group,
                style.fill_hatch,
            )
            label = None
        if style.line_style is not None:
            assert style.line_color is not None
            fig.add_trace(
                go.Scatter(
                    x=x,
                    y=upper,
                    mode="lines",
                    name=labels[i] if labels is not None else f"Component {i + 1}",
                    legendgroup=group,
                    showlegend=label is not None,
                    connectgaps=False,
                    customdata=np.repeat(hists[i].values, 2),
                    hovertemplate=(
                        "%{x}<br>Component: %{customdata}<br>Cumulative: %{y}"
                        "<extra>%{fullData.name}</extra>"
                    ),
                    line=dict(
                        color=_to_rgba(style.line_color, style.line_alpha),
                        width=style.line_width,
                        dash=_LINE_DASH[style.line_style],
                    ),
                )
            )

        total = data.upper[-1]
        x, upper = _staircase(data.edges, total + data.errors)
        _, lower = _staircase(data.edges, total - data.errors)
        _add_fill(
            fig,
            x,
            lower,
            upper,
            "rgba(48,48,48,0.25)",
            "Total ±1σ" if labels is not None else None,
            "stack-total",
        )
    fig.update_layout(
        xaxis_title=hists[0].axes[0].label or None,
        title=hists[0].title or None,
        legend=dict(traceorder="normal", groupclick="togglegroup"),
    )
    return fig

        if scatter.y_label:

def overlay(
    scatters: list[ScatterData],
    labels: list[str] | None = None,
    styles: list[HistogramStyle] | None = None,
) -> go.Figure:
    """Overlay point clouds, using the first dataset's axis labels and title.

    Args:
        scatters: Nonempty list of point clouds.
        labels: Optional legend labels, one per dataset.
        styles: Optional styles, one per dataset; otherwise cycle marker colors.
    """
    if not scatters:
        raise ValueError("scatters must not be empty")
    if labels is not None and len(labels) != len(scatters):
        raise ValueError("labels must have the same length as scatters")
    if styles is not None and len(styles) != len(scatters):
        raise ValueError("styles must have the same length as scatters")
    for scatter in scatters:
        scatter.validate()
    fig = go.Figure()
    for i, scatter in enumerate(scatters):
        color = DEFAULT_COLORS[i % len(DEFAULT_COLORS)]
        style = (
            styles[i]
            if styles is not None
            else HistogramStyle.as_scatter().with_color(color)
        )
        if style.marker_color is None:
            style = style.with_color(color)
        plot(
            scatter,
            style=style,
            label=labels[i] if labels is not None else None,
            fig=fig,
            set_axis_labels=i == 0,
        )
    return fig

def plot(hist: Histogram, max_lines: int = 40) -> str:
    """Render a 1D histogram as a unicode string for terminal output.

    Each bin occupies one character column and the plot height is
    ``max_lines`` rows.  Error bars and spread are intentionally omitted.

    Note:
        Requires a monospace / unicode-capable font in your terminal.
        The plot width equals the number of bins (≤ :data:`MAX_BINS`).

    Args:
        hist:      1D histogram to render.
        max_lines: Height of the plot area in terminal rows (minimum 5).

    Returns:
        A multi-line unicode string.  Pass it to ``print()`` to display.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the data is invalid, has negative values, is not 1D,
                    or has more than :data:`MAX_BINS` bins.
    """
    hist.validate()
    if np.any(hist.values < 0):
        raise ValueError("Terminal backend requires nonnegative bin values")
    if hist.ndim != 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f'Terminal backend only supports 1D histograms, got {hist.ndim}D'
        )
    n_bins = len(hist.axes[0].edges) - 1
    if n_bins > MAX_BINS:
        raise ValueError(
            f'Terminal backend supports at most {MAX_BINS} bins, got {n_bins}'
        )
    return render(
        values_list=[hist.values],
        edges=hist.axes[0].edges,
        max_lines=max_lines,
        title=hist.title or '',
        x_label=hist.axes[0].label or '',
    )
